chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Washa, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Salma, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Two Eids coincided during the era of the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him). So he addressed the people, then said: 'This is a day in which two Eids are gathered. So whoever wishes to join us [in prayer], let him do so, and whoever does not do so, then there is an allowance for him, meaning the one who was laid back [or preferred to stay away].'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling when two Eid festivals fall on the same day?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi records Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) narrating that during the time of Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib, when two Eids coincided, the Imam offered the congregation the choice to join the combined Eid prayer or to exercise a concession (rukhsah) if they preferred not to join, indicating flexibility in communal worship during such occasions. This practice highlights the early Shia adherence to the Sunnah of combining prayers during coinciding festivals, a ruling later elaborated by jurists regarding the necessity of the sermon and the permissibility of individual departure without penalty.
